title: post-onboarding-regression-triage-promptset-heatmap-and-remediations
content:
Summary:

This note captures the triage and proposed remediations for regressions observed in the last two onboarding eval runs (models v1.9 -> v2.1). Rather than a single failure catalog, this write-up organizes failures by operational impact (latency-sensitive misformats vs. correctness regressions) and surface-area (prompt archetype). The goal is to produce fast, testable mitigations for release candidates and a prioritized experimental plan for medium-term fixes.

Background & scope:
- Context: Onboarding eval full run executed 2025-03-04 against the canonical prompt suite (subset: 4k prompts, mixed chat/complete/templates).
- Observed: overall BLEU-like task metrics stable, but discrete regressions concentrated on a few prompt archetypes and downstream parsing failures used by customers.
- Scope of this doc: triage clusters, representative examples, short-term prompt/harness patches, medium-term model and serving changes, and an experiment list with success criteria.

Methodology:
- Error signal sources: token-level diffs vs. golden outputs, parsing failures (JSON/CSV), downstream unit tests failing in integrator harnesses, and user-reported anomalies from CS mock accounts.
- Clustering approach: embed model outputs with a sentence-embedding model (SBERT-mini) and cluster with HDBSCAN + manual merge heuristics. Clusters validated by sampling 30 examples and labeling severity/impact.
- Priority ranking: impact x frequency where impact weights parsing/regression-sensitive customers higher.

Top failure clusters (ranked):

1) Context-truncation: instruction remnants mixed into output (impact: high for structured-output routes)
- Symptom: long system+user histories lead to partial instruction leakage; JSON outputs contain stray "instructions" fields or free text appended to a JSON value.
- Representative prompt archetype: long multi-turn troubleshooting logs + final "produce JSON" instruction.
- Likely cause: KV-cache sharding + length-aware attention causing token-roots to be prefetched from wrong segment; exacerbated by sequence-length bucketing changes in v2.1.

2) Template-entity-swaps (entity aliasing): wrong entity substituted (e.g., customer A inserted where B expected)
- Symptom: names/IDs swapped across templated prompts generated from table-driven test harness.
- Representative archetype: templated prompt with repeated placeholders ({{customer_name}} appears twice with different context windows).
- Likely cause: pointer-decay in position encoding with long repeated placeholders; quantization sensitivity where similar embeddings collapse.

3) Numeric drift & precision loss in arithmetic tasks
- Symptom: off-by-one in totals, rounding differences (2.999 -> 3.5), occasionally producing different units.
- Representative archetype: short calculators and invoice-summarization prompts.
- Likely cause: subtle tokenization shifts and temperature+sampling defaults changed in v2.1 inference config.

4) Format-structure decay in streaming paths
- Symptom: streaming outputs cut off closing brackets or emit trailing partial tokens that downstream parser interprets as errors.
- Representative archetype: streaming JSON responses with nested arrays, consumer reads incomplete chunks.
- Likely cause: streaming buffer flush semantics changed (earlier flush on partial tokens) combined with aggressive min-token flush in runtime.

5) Instruction-erosion for long multi-step instructions
- Symptom: model obeys only the last 1-2 bullets and omits earlier constraints (policy/safety checks often lost).
- Representative archetype: multi-bullet policy transformation prompts where constraints are enumerated.
- Likely cause: attention allocation shifts; rollout of new attention kernel prioritized recency for latency gains.

Quick mitigation proposals (short-term, immediate):
- Patch harness: canonical prompt sanitizer that collapses long histories into compressed summaries before sending to model for any structured-output routes. Implement via lightweight heuristic: keep last 3 turns + summarization instruction. Rollout to canary customers first. Owner: Priya. Target: one-week rollout.
- Strict schema validator pre-commit: accept streaming chunks but buffer until schema-complete heuristics satisfied (e.g., bracket balancing + checksum token). If timeout, request a deterministic retry with deterministic sampling. Owner: Ethan. Target: 3 days.
- Prompt-level disambiguation: when placeholders repeat, explicitly re-label occurrences in prompt (e.g., {{customer_name_1}}, {{customer_name_2}}) to avoid pointer collapse. Add to templating library with warnings. Owner: Diego. Target: 5 days.
- Inference config lockfile: pin sampling/temperature and sequence bucketing settings per onboarding suite to prevent silent drift across infra upgrades. Owner: eng-release. Target: immediate.

Medium term remediations (experiments / 2–8 weeks):
- KV-cache segment boundary test: regression test that injects synthetic long histories to ensure no instruction bleed. If failing, evaluate reverting to previous shard boundaries or applying conservative cache eviction for system messages.
- Quantization-sensitivity sweep: run 3-bit/4-bit/8-bit variants on failing prompt subsets to isolate embeddings collapse. If quantization is root cause, release model-specific quantization profiles for customer-critical prompt archetypes.
- Attention-allocation ablation: instrument attention distribution telemetry to see which tokens lose mass across versions; train small adapter with emphasis loss on early instructions to test mitigation.

Longer term / platform changes (quarter+):
- Prompt archetype fingerprinting: integrate a lightweight fingerprint (hash of abstracted token classes + slot map) so that runtime can route high-risk archetypes to stable model variants or dedicated pools.
- Automated counterfactual patch generation: use prompt-edit-gen agent to propose minimal prompt edits that fix a failing sample; store these as canonical patches for promptsets and CI.
- Model-mix fallback policies: default to more conservative decoding (greedy or low-temp beam) for structured-output routes when schema-violation risk is high.

Experiment plan and metrics:
- Experiments: 1) sanitizer vs. none on structured-output subset; 2) schema-buffer vs. streaming immediate; 3) quantization sweep for template-entity-swaps.
- Metrics: schema-violation rate (primary), downstream integration test pass rate, mean time to first byte (latency impact), cost delta per 1k tokens.
- Success criteria: reduce schema-violation rate by >= 70% on failing archetypes with <= 10% latency degradation for hosted API canned customers; for Dedicated flag, accept up to 25% latency if bounded and documented.

Rollout & monitoring:
- Canary cohort: 10% of non-enterprise traffic for 48 hours for sanitizer + schema-buffer. Escalate if schema violations drop and latency delta < 8%.
- Dashboard: add a per-archetype timeseries (heatmap) to Console Optimize: weekly regression alert when any archetype shows +10% delta in violation rate.

Action items (owners & tickets):
- Priya: implement prompt sanitizer + PR to templating lib (JIRA-ML-4821).
- Ethan: streaming schema buffer heuristic + integration tests (JIRA-ML-4830).
- Diego: update templating docs, add placeholder disambiguation lint rule (GH PR in linked_artifacts).
- Maya (owner consolidator): run quantization sweep and collect results by 2025-04-01.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we prioritize latency-preserving attention kernel (current) or correctness (older kernel) for Dedicated pools? (Decision req: Product/Infra tradeoff).
- Should we provide customers an explicit "structured-output" flag that enforces conservative decoding and schema buffering?

Appendix: representative failing samples (anonymized) and quick repro steps:
- Sample A (context-truncation): reproduce by sending 12-turn dialog + final "return JSON" instruction. Compare outputs between v1.9 and v2.1; v2.1 includes a stray 'instruction' field.
- Sample B (entity-swap): templated prompt with repeated {{account}} placeholders and two different replacement values; run through templater and compare substitution order and model output.

References:
- linked artifacts: CONFLUENCE-ENG/Onboarding-Evals, JIRA-ML-4821, github PR referenced above.

Notes and next sync:
- We'll sync on 2025-03-20 10:00 with eng-applied-ml + release to align pinning policy. Please add any other failing samples to the shared sheet: /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/onboard-failures-2025-03 (internal).
